short: The last Tudor monarch, whose 44-year reign steadied a divided England.
full:
Elizabeth I acceded in November 1558, aged twenty-five, inheriting a kingdom bankrupted by war and split by two decades of violent religious reversal. Her Religious Settlement of 1559 deliberately blurred doctrine enough to be liveable for most of her subjects — a pragmatic compromise that held.

Her reign saw the defeat of the Spanish Armada in 1588, the first English colonial ventures, and the theatre of Marlowe and Shakespeare. She never married, using the prospect of her hand as a diplomatic instrument for decades. She died in March 1603, and the crown passed to James VI of Scotland, uniting the two crowns.
